title: Ancient Roman Calendar Notation
intro: Ancient Roman date notation names a day relative to a month landmark rather than numbering forward from the first day.
structure: Kalends are the first day of every month. Nones are the fifth and Ides the thirteenth, except in March, May, July and October, where they are the seventh and fifteenth. Other dates count backward inclusively from the next landmark, including the landmark itself.
model: The provider uses proleptic Julian month/day arithmetic and renders the appropriate landmark and inclusive countdown. It is a notation layer over the Julian day coordinate.
example: 15 March is the Ides of March; 14 March is the day before the Ides (pridie Idus Martias); 13 March is the third day before the Ides by inclusive counting.
history: Kalends, Nones and Ides were established Roman civic reference dates and occur throughout Latin historical writing.
limits: This is not a reconstruction of the pre-Julian calendar's intercalations, early regnal chronology or irregular early leap-day administration.
